questions.text: A sum of ₹5,000 is invested at 8% per annum simple interest for 3 years. What is the total interest earned?
questions.explanation: SI = P × R × T / 100 = 5000 × 8 × 3 / 100 = 1200. Total amount = 5000 + 1200 = ₹6,200. Common error: multiplying rate by years but forgetting to divide by 100.

questions.text: At what rate of simple interest will ₹4,000 amount to ₹5,200 in 4 years?
₹6,000 is invested at 10% per annum compounded annually for 2 years. What is the compound interest earned?
questions.explanation: A = P(1 + r/100)^n = 6000 × (1.1)² = 6000 × 1.21 = 7260. CI = 7260 − 6000 = ₹1,260. Simple interest would have been 6000 × 10 × 2/100 = ₹1,200. The extra ₹60 is interest-on-interest.

questions.text: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹8,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years is ____.
questions.explanation: For 2 years, CI − SI = P × (R/100)² = 8000 × (5/100)² = 8000 × 0.0025 = ₹20. This formula is the shortcut for any 2-year problem: the difference equals P × r²/10000.

questions.text: A sum doubles itself at simple interest in 8 years. In how many years will the same sum become 4 times at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Doubles in 8 years → SI equals principal in 8 years → R = 100/(8) = 12.5% pa. For amount = 4P, SI = 3P. Time = (3P × 100)/(P × 12.5) = 24 years. Shortcut: to become 4P, need 3× the principal as interest = 3 × 8 = 24 years.

questions.text: ₹10,000 is invested at 20% per annum compounded half-yearly for 1 year. What is the total amount at the end of 1 year?
questions.explanation: Half-yearly: rate per period = 20/2 = 10%; periods = 1 × 2 = 2. A = 10000 × (1.10)² = 10000 × 1.21 = ₹12,100. Trap: annual compounding would give 10000 × 1.20 = ₹12,000. Half-yearly compounding gives ₹100 more due to more frequent compounding.

questions.text: A person borrows ₹15,000 at 12% per annum simple interest and repays ₹21,600 after some years. How many years did he hold the loan?

options.option_text: 3 years exactly at this interest rate
4 years exactly at this interest rate
5 years exactly at this interest rate
